chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, from ignorance is laughter without wonderment (or cause).
And he (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Do not show off your teeth in laughter when you have committed disgraceful deeds, and one who commits evil deeds is not secure from being caught overnight.'

key_terms.الْوَاضِحَةٍ: The obvious one (referring to the teeth)

ai.seo_question: What does Shia hadith say about the relationship between laughter and ignorance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies unprovoked or excessive laughter as a sign of ignorance, linking it to a lack of self-awareness and spiritual depth. He further advises that those who have committed shameful deeds should not display their teeth in laughter, as their evil actions may catch them by surprise during the night, illustrating the concept of *ghurur* (deception by worldly ease). This hadith serves as a reminder to maintain dignity and mindfulness even in moments of joy.
